title: cornfield v1: sign-in, forges, PR-comment reviews, the issues and PRs panel
summary: Forge sign-in (admins only, on the server), a SQLite file, GitHub and Forgejo adapters, reviews posted as spec-PR comments, proposals read from spec branches, and a panel of issues and PRs that points into the map.

add.label: auth.js
add.desc: Sign-in with GitHub or Forgejo (OAuth), sessions in an HttpOnly cookie, and the admins-only guard every route passes through.

add.label: db.js
add.desc: The SQLite file in the data folder (node:sqlite): sessions, reviews, the audit of actions, forge caches; numbered migrations.

add.label: forge.js
add.desc: The forge adapter interface: who you are, your permission on the repo, issues, pull requests, files, comments, checks, branches, file contents at a ref.

add.label: reviews.js
add.desc: Approve / Send back as a spec-PR comment (a human line and a fenced cornfield-review JSON block); the latest admin comment is the review.

add.label: forge-panel.js
add.desc: The issues and PRs panel for both forges. A PR lights the nodes its files are; a failing check lights its tests.

add.label: cornfield.db
add.desc: cornfield's own SQLite file, in its data folder, never in a checkout.

add.label: Forgejo
add.breaks: Now: a Forgejo-hosted repo's sign-in, issues, PRs and reviews stop; the map still shows.
add.desc: A Forgejo instance, when the config's forge is one: sign-in, issues, pull requests, comments, checks.

set.desc: The HTTP server: every route behind the sign-in guard; the loopback rule lifts once sign-in is configured with an https public URL.

change.why: sign-in guards every route, and binding beyond loopback is allowed only with it

set.desc: The proposal routes: proposals from open spec PRs and from the worktrees folder; a review is posted to the spec PR, never written into a checkout.

change.why: reviews move from the data folder to PR comments

set.desc: Approve and Send back on the proposal bar: the review goes to the spec PR as a comment, and the bar shows the latest one.

change.why: the review is a PR comment

scenarios.title: A maintainer signs in and sees the map

steps.text: You open cornfield. Nothing is shown before you sign in: the server answers every route with the sign-in page.
You choose to sign in with the repo's forge.
The forge says who you are and that you maintain the repo.
Your session is kept in cornfield's own SQLite file.

scenarios.title: Someone without maintainer rights signs in

steps.text: The forge says they can read the repo but do not maintain it.
They see one page: this is the dev dashboard; ask a maintainer. topology.json, the proposals and every API answer 403 for them.

scenarios.title: Approving a proposal posts on its spec PR

steps.text: You open a proposal from the Proposals menu, which lists the open spec PRs, and press Approve with a note.
The server turns it into a comment: one line for people, a cornfield-review JSON block for the agent.
The comment lands on the spec PR. Nothing is written into a checkout.
The bar shows: Approved just now. The latest comment wins.

scenarios.title: A PR lights the nodes it changes

steps.text: You pick a PR in the issues and PRs panel.
The server asks the forge for the PR's files and checks.
Each file is matched to the node that holds it; those nodes light up, and a failing check lights its test files.
